brief.title: Data Augmentation Impact on CNN: Fashion-MNIST
brief.summary: This study trains a small convolutional neural network on Fashion-MNIST under two controlled conditions — standard training and training with basic image augmentations — holding all other hyperparameters fixed. Each condition is run with two random seeds (42 and 123) to provide modest reproducibility evidence without overstating statistical significance. The experiment measures test accuracy, training curves, and validation performance to determine whether simple augmentation meaningfully improves generalization.
scope_in: Fashion-MNIST dataset (60 000 train / 10 000 test split)
Small CNN implemented in PyTorch (two or three conv blocks + fully connected head)
Two training conditions: no augmentation vs. random horizontal flip + small random translation (up to 10%) + minor rotation (up to 10°)
5 training epochs per condition
Random seeds 42 and 123 for both conditions
Identical architecture, optimizer (Adam or SGD with fixed LR), batch size, and train/validation split across conditions
GPU training on Google Colab T4 or L4 via CUDA, with logged evidence of GPU detection
Test accuracy, per-epoch training loss, and validation accuracy curves
Summary table comparing conditions and seeds
Figures: learning curves per condition, bar chart of final test accuracies
scope_out: Architectures other than the single small CNN
Augmentation strategies beyond the three specified transforms (no Cutout, Mixup, AutoAugment, etc.)
Statistical significance testing (e.g., t-tests) given only two seeds
CPU-only training runs as substitutes for GPU runs
assumptions: Optimizer assumed to be Adam with a fixed learning rate of 1e-3 (a standard sensible default for small CNNs on Fashion-MNIST), as the user did not specify one explicitly.
Train/validation split assumed to be 90/10 of the 60 000 training images (54 000 train, 6 000 validation), a common practical choice.
CNN architecture assumed to consist of two convolutional blocks (Conv→ReLU→MaxPool) followed by a two-layer fully connected head, balancing speed and capacity for Fashion-MNIST.
Batch size assumed to be 64, a widely used default that fits comfortably on a T4/L4 GPU.
Augmentations are applied only at training time; the validation and test sets use only normalization (mean/std of Fashion-MNIST).

clarification.content:
Research question: Does simple data augmentation improve the test accuracy of a convolutional neural network on Fashion-MNIST?

Keep the research relatively simple, scientifically rigorous, and computationally manageable. The study should investigate whether applying basic image augmentation during training improves a CNN's generalization performance compared with training the same CNN without augmentation.

Experimental requirements:
- Dataset: Fashion-MNIST.
- Framework: PyTorch.
- Model: A small CNN suitable for fast training.
- Conditions: Standard training versus training with basic image augmentation.
- Augmentation: Use simple, reasonable transformations such as small random translations or rotations.
- Training: Approximately 5 epochs per condition.
- Random seeds: 42 and 123, for both conditions.
- Keep the architecture, optimizer, learning rate, training/validation split, and other relevant hyperparameters identical between conditions.
- Evaluate test accuracy, training/validation performance, and differences between conditions.
- Generate relevant experimental figures and tables.
- Do not overstate statistical significance with only two seeds.
- Use real literature sources, real computations, and real experimental outputs.
- Compute: the neural network training runs must execute on a CUDA GPU through Google Colab (T4 or L4) using the GPU job tool, and must record evidence that PyTorch detected the CUDA GPU and trained on it. Do not substitute CPU training. Ordinary Python, data processing and plotting may run in the regular CPU sandbox.

Keep the project focused. Do not expand it into a large hyperparameter search or extensive benchmark study.

themes.name: CNN Architectures and Baselines on Fashion-MNIST
themes.description: A large body of work benchmarks various CNN designs on Fashion-MNIST, from simple sequential CNNs to deeper multi-block architectures. These papers establish the performance landscape against which augmentation gains can be measured.

themes.name: Effect of Data Augmentation on CNN Generalization
themes.description: These papers directly study how standard image augmentations (flips, rotations, translations, crops) affect CNN training and test performance. They provide empirical evidence that even simple augmentations meaningfully reduce overfitting and improve accuracy.

themes.name: Augmentation Techniques: Surveys and Taxonomy
themes.description: Comprehensive surveys cataloguing the breadth of augmentation strategies, from classical geometric transforms to GAN-based and meta-learning approaches. These papers contextualize the three simple augmentations used in this experiment within the wider space of options.

themes.name: Optimizer, Regularization, and Hyperparameter Interactions
themes.description: These papers examine how optimizer choice (Adam, SGD), dropout, batch normalization, and hyperparameter tuning interact with augmentation to affect CNN performance. Relevant because the experiment fixes optimizer and hyperparameters to isolate augmentation effects.

themes.name: Fashion-MNIST Augmentation and High-Accuracy Results
themes.description: Papers that specifically combine augmentation with CNN training on Fashion-MNIST and report high accuracy results, directly relevant as upper-bound benchmarks and as evidence that augmentation helps on this exact dataset.

themes.name: Augmentation Effects Across Domains and Datasets
themes.description: Papers applying augmentation to diverse domains (medical, satellite, plant, defect detection) that collectively reinforce the generality of augmentation benefits while also showing dataset-specific variation in what augmentations help most.

themes.name: Lightweight CNN Design and Reproducibility in PyTorch
themes.description: Papers focusing on building and evaluating small, efficient CNN models in frameworks like PyTorch, addressing practical concerns of training speed, reproducibility across seeds, and controlled experimental design.

overview.summary:
The field of CNN-based image classification on Fashion-MNIST is well-established, with reported test accuracies ranging from ~88% for simple architectures to near 99.65% for optimized, augmented models. Data augmentation — including flips, translations, rotations, and more exotic methods — is broadly shown to improve generalization, reduce overfitting, and push accuracy higher, particularly when training data is limited or the model is small. The literature consistently demonstrates that even basic geometric augmentations (the focus of this experiment) provide measurable accuracy gains over unaugmented baselines.

However, the field increasingly moves beyond simple augmentations toward advanced strategies (Mixup, CutMix, AutoAugment) and larger architectures (ResNets, ViTs), making it harder to isolate the specific contribution of simple augmentation on small CNNs. Most published work does not run controlled two-condition experiments with fixed seeds, making direct comparisons across studies difficult. This experiment's controlled design — holding architecture, optimizer, and hyperparameters fixed while varying only augmentation — directly addresses a gap in reproducible, minimal-footprint benchmarking on Fashion-MNIST.
open_problems: Isolating the contribution of individual augmentation types (e.g., flips vs. rotations vs. translations) without confounding from other design choices
Determining how augmentation benefits scale with model size — whether small CNNs benefit more or less than larger architectures
Lack of standardized controlled experiments: most papers vary multiple factors simultaneously, making attribution of accuracy gains to augmentation alone difficult
Reproducibility across random seeds is rarely reported with more than one or two seeds, leaving statistical reliability of results unclear
Optimal augmentation magnitude (degree of rotation, translation range) is dataset- and architecture-dependent and rarely systematically searched for simple CNNs
Generalization from benchmark datasets like Fashion-MNIST to real-world fashion images remains a persistent gap
Whether gains from simple augmentations plateau quickly with more training epochs, and whether 5 epochs is sufficient to observe the full effect
common_methods: Train/validation/test splits with fixed random seeds

papers.venue: International Journal of Recent Technology and Engineering (IJRTE)

notes.problem: How do hyperparameter optimization methods and regularization techniques affect CNN performance on the Fashion-MNIST benchmark?
limitations: No comparison with state-of-the-art results reported with specific numbers
Limited to a single dataset
notes.contribution: Explores hyperparameter optimization and regularization techniques for CNN-based image classification on Fashion-MNIST with data augmentation.
key_findings: Proposed deep ConvNet architectures with data augmentation achieve impressive results on Fashion-MNIST
Data augmentation techniques such as cropping, rotation, flipping, and shifting help address insufficient training samples

papers.venue: International Conference on Image Information Processing (ICIIP)

notes.problem: How to accurately classify fashion article images using deep learning.
notes.contribution: Three CNN architectures with batch normalization and residual skip connections achieving ~2% accuracy improvement on Fashion-MNIST classification.
key_findings: Proposed CNN models achieve ~2% accuracy improvement over existing state-of-the-art on Fashion-MNIST.

papers.title: Revolutionizing Digit Image Recognition: Pushing the Limits with Simple CNN and Challenging Image Augmentation Techniques on MNIST

notes.problem: How can image augmentation techniques improve CNN-based handwritten digit recognition accuracy?
limitations: Evaluated only on MNIST; more challenging datasets not explored
CNN architecture improvements not investigated in this work
notes.contribution: Applies CNN with image augmentation techniques to achieve 99.81% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition.
key_findings: CNN with image augmentation achieved maximum accuracy of 99.81% on MNIST
Ensemble of CNN models achieved 99.79% accuracy
Image augmentation techniques effectively reduced overfitting and improved performance

papers.title: Image Classification Using Multiple Convolutional Neural Networks on the Fashion-MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: How to accurately classify fashion/clothing images for robotic manipulation in household and elderly-care settings.
limitations: Low accuracy on real-world household dataset (40%) suggests limited generalization
Custom household dataset is small and not publicly described in detail
notes.contribution: Proposes MCNN15, a 15-layer convolutional neural network that achieves 94.04% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, outperforming prior state-of-the-art for clothing classification in service robotics.
key_findings: MCNN15 achieved 94.04% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, boosting state-of-the-art
MCNN15 achieved 60% accuracy on Fashion-Product dataset
MCNN15 achieved 40% accuracy on customized household dataset

papers.title: Classification of Fashion-MNIST Dataset by Using Lenet-5
papers.venue: Science and Technology of Engineering Chemistry and Environmental Protection

notes.problem: How effective is the classic LeNet-5 architecture on the Fashion-MNIST dataset for clothing image classification?
limitations: Only one model (LeNet-5) evaluated without comparison to more modern architectures
notes.contribution: Applies LeNet-5 CNN to Fashion-MNIST image classification and evaluates its effectiveness as a benchmark task.
key_findings: LeNet-5 achieves 95% training accuracy on Fashion-MNIST
LeNet-5 achieves 90% validation accuracy, indicating good generalization

papers.title: State-of-the-Art Results with the Fashion-MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: How well can classical ML models and simple CNNs classify Fashion-MNIST images, and how does the number of trainable parameters affect classification quality?
limitations: Experiments limited to Fashion-MNIST; generalizability to other datasets not demonstrated
notes.contribution: A CNN with three convolutional layers (CNN-3-128) achieves 99.65% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, setting a new state-of-the-art result.
key_findings: CNN-3-128 achieved 99.65% accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST test set
There is a dependence between the number of adjustable parameters in a CNN and the maximum achievable classification quality

papers.title: Classification of Standard FASHION MNIST Dataset Using Deep Learning Based CNN Algorithms
papers.venue: International Symposium on Multidisciplinary Studies and Innovative Technologies (ISMSIT)

notes.problem: How to improve CNN-based image classification on Fashion MNIST while mitigating model overfitting.
limitations: Only two custom architectures compared; no benchmark against well-known models like ResNet or VGG
notes.contribution: Two CNN architectures (CNN-C1 and CNN-C2) are proposed and compared for Fashion MNIST image classification, with CNN-C2 achieving 93.11% accuracy.
key_findings: CNN-C2 outperforms CNN-C1 and achieves 93.11% accuracy on Fashion MNIST

papers.title: CNN-Based Image Classification on the Fashion-MNIST Dataset
papers.venue: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence
authors: Abdul Salam Shah Sayed Chia Chen Yee

notes.problem: How well does a standard CNN architecture classify grayscale fashion images across ten categories with high intra- and inter-class visual similarity?
limitations: Single relatively simple architecture evaluated
No data augmentation applied
Attention-based or more complex architectures not explored
notes.contribution: Empirical evaluation of a sequential CNN for multi-class image classification on Fashion-MNIST achieving 88.85% test accuracy
key_findings: Achieved 88.85% test accuracy with no major overfitting
Morphologically distinctive categories (trousers, bags, footwear) showed high discriminative performance
Systematic inter-class confusion observed among upper-body garments (shirts, T-shirts, pullovers)

papers.title: Optimized Neural Networks for Fashion-MNIST: A High-Accuracy Approach Using Augmentation and Tuning
papers.venue: International Mobile, Intelligent, and Ubiquitous Computing Conference (MIUCC)

notes.problem: How can CNN-based architectures be optimized to maximize classification accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST benchmark?
notes.contribution: A ResCNN architecture with residual blocks, modified design, and hyperparameter tuning achieves 98.30% test accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, surpassing prior CNN-based results by 4%.
key_findings: ResCNN achieved 98.30% test accuracy on Fashion-MNIST
This surpasses previous CNN-based literature on Fashion-MNIST by 4%
Residual blocks, modified architecture, and hyperparameter tuning contributed to performance gains

papers.title: Synergizing CNNs and ViTs
papers.venue: Revista de Informática Teórica e Aplicada

notes.problem: How can CNNs and ViTs be combined to improve accuracy, scalability, and interpretability in fashion image classification?
limitations: Review scope limited to Fashion MNIST benchmark, which may not fully represent real-world complexity
notes.contribution: A survey of hybrid CNN-ViT architectures for clothing classification, with emphasis on the Fashion MNIST benchmark and model explainability.
key_findings: Hybrid CNN-ViT models outperform individual CNN or ViT architectures on fashion classification tasks
Hybrid models enhance interpretability compared to standalone architectures

papers.title: A survey on Image Data Augmentation for Deep Learning

notes.problem: Deep learning models require large datasets to avoid overfitting, but many domains like medical imaging have limited data.
limitations: No empirical comparisons performed; findings are based on surveyed literature
notes.contribution: A comprehensive survey of image data augmentation techniques for deep learning, covering geometric, color, GAN-based, and meta-learning approaches.
key_findings: Data augmentation can improve model performance and expand limited datasets
GAN-based augmentation methods are a promising direction for generating realistic training samples
Test-time augmentation, resolution, dataset size, and curriculum learning are important meta-level considerations

papers.title: Classification of Garments from Fashion MNIST Dataset Using CNN LeNet-5 Architecture

notes.problem: Classifying clothing items from images is challenging due to high inter-class similarity and complex category depth
notes.contribution: Applies LeNet-5 CNN architecture to Fashion MNIST garment classification, achieving over 98% accuracy
key_findings: LeNet-5 achieved over 98% accuracy on Fashion MNIST
LeNet-5 outperformed classical CNN and other state-of-the-art models in the literature

papers.title: A Convolutional Neural Network for Leaves Recognition Using Data Augmentation

notes.problem: How to effectively classify plant leaves using deep learning while mitigating overfitting on small datasets.
limitations: Evaluated on only one dataset (Flavia).
notes.contribution: A 7-layer CNN with data augmentation (rotation, translation, sharpening) for plant leaf recognition that outperforms prior methods on the Flavia dataset.
key_findings: The proposed 7-layer CNN with data augmentation outperforms other supervised learning methods on the Flavia leaf dataset.
Data augmentation via rotation, translation, and random sharpening reduces overfitting and improves generalization.

notes.problem: How do regularization strategies such as dropout and data augmentation affect overfitting and generalization across different CNN architectures?
limitations: Only one dataset (Imagenette) used
Limited to dropout and data augmentation; other regularization methods not evaluated
Resource-constrained environments not tested
notes.contribution: Systematic comparison of dropout and data augmentation regularization techniques on generalization in baseline CNNs vs. ResNet-18 for image classification
key_findings: ResNet-18 achieved 82.37% validation accuracy vs. 68.74% for the baseline CNN
Regularization reduced overfitting and improved generalization across all tested architectures
Transfer learning led to faster convergence and higher accuracy than training from scratch

papers.title: Building Efficient Lightweight CNN Models

notes.problem: How to build CNNs that maintain competitive accuracy while meeting the computational and memory constraints of resource-limited environments.
limitations: Lower performance on complex datasets like CIFAR-10
Methodology evaluated only on classification tasks
Architectural scalability for more complex datasets needs further improvement
notes.contribution: A two-stage training methodology combining dual-input-output models and transfer learning with progressive unfreezing to build lightweight CNNs with competitive accuracy.
key_findings: Achieved 99% accuracy on MNIST and 89% on Fashion-MNIST with only 14,862 parameters and 0.17 MB model size.
CIFAR-10 accuracy was 65% with fewer than 20,000 parameters, showing scalability limits on complex datasets.
Progressive unfreezing enabled faster convergence and improved accuracy during fine-tuning.

papers.title: Prediction of Most Confident Labelled Output for Fashion Image using Deep Learning Model with Tensorflow

notes.problem: How to accurately classify fashion images despite high variability in clothing attributes such as designs, textures, and colours.
limitations: Evaluated only on Fashion-MNIST; generalizability to other fashion datasets not shown
notes.contribution: Proposes the Most Confident Labelled Output (MCLO) algorithm combined with CNN optimizers for fashion image classification using TensorFlow/GPU.
key_findings: AdaGrad optimizer achieved the best accuracy and lowest loss among the tested CNN optimizers
The proposed MCLO algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art models on the Fashion-MNIST benchmark

papers.title: Tradeoffs in Data Augmentation: An Empirical Study

notes.problem: How can the effect of data augmentation on model generalization be measured and understood?
notes.contribution: Introduces two measures, Affinity and Diversity, to quantify how data augmentation improves model generalization.
key_findings: Affinity and Diversity capture a tradeoff in data augmentation that predicts generalization performance
Higher diversity augmentations improve generalization but too low affinity can hurt performance

papers.title: Reducing Overfitting and Improving Generalization in Training Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) under Limited Sample Sizes in Image Recognition

notes.problem: How to reduce overfitting and improve generalization when training CNNs with limited sample sizes.
limitations: Study limited to a single dataset (contracted CIFAR-10)
Specific epoch injection timing may not generalize to other architectures or datasets
notes.contribution: Demonstrates that injecting width/height shift data augmentation at epoch 30 combined with dropout yields the best performance for reducing overfitting in CNN image recognition under limited samples.
key_findings: Injecting data augmentation at epoch 30 with width and height shift combined with dropout yields the best performance against overfitting.
Combination of techniques outperforms individual techniques for generalization under limited data.

limitations: Single CNN architecture evaluated without comparison to transfer learning or ensemble models
No real-time or video classification tested
Relatively small and potentially imbalanced custom dataset

key_findings: Model achieved ~82% test accuracy after 25 epochs
